# SQ-1600: a verified command sequence for The Hitchhiker's Guide to the
# Galaxy (hitchhiker-r59-s851108.z3, v3 Z-code), reconstructed by booting the
# real game headlessly and driving it turn by turn, checking every reply
# against the actual interpreter. This is NOT a copy of any published
# walkthrough's prose -- it is this project's own derived list of literal
# game commands, produced for automated regression testing
# (crates/app/tests/suites/walkthrough_hhgg.rs).
#
# Derived with the aid of, as a guide only (never transcribed):
#   hitchhiker.txt, IF Archive, Scorpia, 06-Dec-1992
#   https://www.ifarchive.org/if-archive/infocom/hints/solutions/hitchhiker.txt
#   hitchhiker.step, IF Archive, Doug Howell / Peter van Turennout, 17-Dec-1992
#   https://www.ifarchive.org/if-archive/infocom/hints/solutions/hitchhiker.step
#
# Format: one command per line; blank lines and `#`-comment lines are
# ignored. A line submitted while the game is at a single-keypress (Char)
# prompt is sent as a keypress (its first character); otherwise it is
# submitted as an ordinary typed line.
#
# WHY THIS SCRIPT IS LONG (~600 commands): after the Babel-fish/poetry/
# airlock opening, the game boards you on the Heart of Gold and the middle
# act is driven by pushing the spare Improbability Drive's switch, which
# throws you into one of several first-person flashback vignettes chosen by
# the game's own hidden state each time (Bugblatter Beast, Trillian, Ford,
# the Vl'hurg/G'Gugvunt War Room, Zaphod, and eventually the whale's-tummy
# scene) -- the game's own manual documents this as unpredictable ("it may
# take more than one try to get here, but you will make it eventually").
# zvm's Z-machine `random` opcode is seeded from a fixed constant with no OS
# entropy at initial boot (`Machine::DEFAULT_RNG_SEED`), so a fresh boot
# always draws the identical sequence turn-for-turn -- which is what makes
# this script reproducible at all despite the game's own randomness. Getting
# from "all five vignettes done" to the whale's tummy took several retries
# (the game revisits already-completed vignettes before landing on a new
# one), and ONE of the wrong turns (revisiting the Vl'hurg/G'Gugvunt War
# Room's time-paradox maze a second time) is scripted to kill you outright
# about five turns later NO MATTER WHAT YOU DO -- confirmed by letting it
# play out once. So this script deliberately routes around a second visit
# to that specific flashback: whenever "you hear ... a star drive ... from
# far below" is followed by a bare `aft` leading straight back into it, the
# fix is to `wait` and `listen` again rather than take that exit, which
# lets the RNG re-roll instead of walking into the guaranteed-fatal branch.
#
# Never repeat the war-room/maze flashback via a direct `aft` off a
# "far below" listen after it has already been completed once.
